device.name: SESAME Smart Locks (SESAME 3/4/5/5 PRO, Bot 2, bike 2)
device.notes:
SESAME locks by CANDY HOUSE are unusually developer-friendly: the vendor PUBLISHES the full SesameOS3 BLE protocol and ships open-source SDKs (the vendor app runs on the same SDK). Full local BLE lock/unlock/history works with no vendor cloud once the per-device secret is held; the cloud/AWS-IoT is only for remote access.
ADVERTISEMENT: service 0xFD81; a 31-byte packet with manufacturer data under company id 0x055A (1370) carrying a product model code (0 = Sesame 3, 4 = Sesame 4, 5 = Sesame 5, 17 = Sesame Bot 2), a status byte and the 16-byte device UUID, plus the complete-16-bit-service-UUID field (03 03 81 FD).
GATT: write (commands) 16860002-a5ae-9856-b6d3-dbb4c676993e; notify (responses/publishes) 16860003-a5ae-9856-b6d3-dbb4c676993e. Transport is 20-byte segments; the first header byte bit0 is a start flag and the upper bits are the type: 0x01 plaintext-start, 0x02 plaintext-end, 0x03 plaintext-single, 0x04 ciphertext-end, 0x05 ciphertext-single. Message op types: 0x07 Response, 0x08 Publish.
ITEM/COMMAND CODES: 1 Registration, 2 Login, 4 History, 5 Version, 8 Time-update, 14 Initialization, 80 Mech-settings, 81 Mech-status, 82 Lock, 83 Unlock, 104 Reset.
CRYPTO: key agreement is SECP256R1 ECDH between app and device at Registration; the first 16 bytes of the shared secret become the symmetric device_secret. A 16-byte session token = AES-CMAC(device_secret, random_code) where random_code is a 4-byte value the device publishes at init. Payloads are AES-CCM with a 13-byte IV = counter(8) + nonce(1) + random_code(4) and a 4-byte auth tag. Login enforces a ±3 s time-sync before encrypted traffic.

openness.notes: Officially published and independently re-implemented (libsesame3bt-core). Nothing was reverse-engineered; upstream is authoritative.

credentials.notes: Per-device ECDH secret + AES-CCM with a timestamp check resists trivial replay. No Wi-Fi on the lock (a separate Wi-Fi module / hub provides remote access). No public advisory surfaced.

factory_reset.effect: Item code 104 (Reset) returns the lock to unregistered state, clearing the device_secret and settings. A physical reset button also exists on the hardware.

procedures.basis: Documented in the SesameOS3 protocol (item code 104); not replayed by this project.
procedures.name: Reset command (item 104)

steps.action: Send the Reset command (item 104) over an authenticated session, or use the hardware reset button.
steps.expect: The lock returns to unregistered state.

methods.description: Register (ECDH) to obtain the device_secret, then Login (establish the AES-CMAC session token, sync time within ±3 s) and send Lock (82) / Unlock (83) as AES-CCM ciphertext segments on the write characteristic. The Registration/ECDH step is a genuine pairing/provisioning flow, not plain connect-and-go.

steps.action: Register: perform SECP256R1 ECDH with the lock to derive the device_secret (or load it from the printed QR on SESAME 5).
Login: derive the session token AES-CMAC(device_secret, random_code); sync the clock within ±3 s.
Send Lock (82) / Unlock (83) as AES-CCM segments to 16860002; read responses on 16860003.

setup.notes: Registration is an in-app ECDH pairing that mints the per-device device_secret (for SESAME 5-class hardware the secret can also come from the printed QR). After that, local control needs only the device_secret and a ±3 s time sync. Confidence high: officially documented and independently implemented.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a client with the device_secret re-connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The service/characteristic UUIDs, segment framing, item codes and the ECDH/AES-CCM crypto are from CANDY HOUSE's own SesameOS3 documentation, corroborated by the independent libsesame3bt-core ESP32 implementation.
